subtopics.title: Insolation and the Earth's Heat Budget

questions.question: Of 100 units of insolation, the approximate split used in the lesson is:
options: 30 reflected back to space, 20 absorbed by the atmosphere, 50 absorbed at the earth's surface
50 reflected, 30 absorbed by the atmosphere, 20 at the surface

questions.question: Albedo is:
options: The heat stored in the oceans
The proportion of insolation REFLECTED back to space — high for snow, ice and pale desert soils, low for dark ocean and forest
The rate at which temperature falls with height
The total energy the sun emits

questions.question: The earth radiates energy back to space as LONG-WAVE radiation because:
options: The earth is far cooler than the sun, so its emitted radiation is of longer wavelength — and the atmosphere absorbs long-wave well

questions.question: Global winds and ocean currents exist chiefly because:
options: The tropics run a permanent energy SURPLUS and the polar regions a permanent DEFICIT, and the imbalance must be transferred

subtopics.title: How Heat Moves — Radiation, Conduction, Convection, Advection

questions.question: The transfer of heat HORIZONTALLY by moving air — for example a sea breeze at Muizenberg or a berg wind reaching the coast — is:
Conduction matters only in the lowest few metres of the atmosphere because:
options: Air is a POOR CONDUCTOR, so molecule-to-molecule transfer reaches no further than the air actually in contact with the ground

questions.question: A convection current is established when:
options: Air warmed at the surface expands, becomes less dense and rises, while cooler denser air sinks to replace it

questions.question: The single most important consequence in this section is that the atmosphere is heated:
options: Directly by the sun's short-wave radiation
FROM BELOW — insolation passes largely through the air, warms the ground, and the ground then heats the air, which is why temperature falls with height in the troposphere

subtopics.title: The Greenhouse Effect and Enhanced Warming

questions.question: The correct order of the greenhouse mechanism is:
options: Short-wave passes through → absorbed by the surface → re-radiated as long-wave → absorbed by greenhouse gases → re-radiated in all directions including back down
Long-wave passes through → absorbed by clouds → reflected to space
Short-wave absorbed by greenhouse gases → radiated to space
Ozone absorbs long-wave → the surface cools

questions.question: The NATURAL greenhouse effect is necessary because without it the global average surface temperature would be about:
options: −18 °C instead of about 15 °C — some 33 degrees of habitability

questions.question: Which list gives human sources of the ENHANCED greenhouse effect?
options: Volcanic eruptions and ocean currents only
Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, livestock and rice agriculture, landfills, and cement manufacture

questions.question: Which is NOT given in the lesson as a consequence of climate change for Africa?
options: Less reliable rainfall and longer droughts in the south and west
Falling maize yields and threatened food security
Malarial mosquitoes moving into higher, cooler areas
A thinning of the ozone layer over the Antarctic

subtopics.title: The Five Factors That Set Temperature

questions.question: Temperature falls from equator to poles because at high latitudes the sun's rays:
options: Strike obliquely, so the same beam spreads over a larger area AND travels a longer, more absorbing path through the atmosphere
Are weaker when they leave the sun
Are blocked by the ozone layer

questions.question: Johannesburg sits near 1 750 m. Using a lapse rate of 6,5 °C per 1 000 m, the temperature fall due to altitude alone is about:
The sea moderates coastal temperatures mainly because water:
options: Heats and cools far more slowly than land — it is transparent, mixes by currents and waves, loses heat to evaporation and needs more energy per degree — so coastal places have a SMALL annual temperature range

questions.question: The correct pairing of South Africa's currents is:
options: Cold Agulhas on the east, warm Benguela on the west
Warm Benguela on the east, cold Agulhas on the west
Warm AGULHAS flowing south down the east coast, giving Durban warmth, humidity and summer rain; cold BENGUELA flowing north up the west coast, giving Port Nolloth cool, dry, foggy conditions

questions.question: In the hundred-rand story, the thirty rand that 'never gets spent' represents:
options: The albedo — energy reflected straight back off cloud tops, dust and bright surfaces

questions.question: The 'twist that explains the whole topic' is that the ground:
options: Spends the energy back upward in a DIFFERENT currency — long-wave instead of short-wave — and the atmosphere grabs long-wave greedily on the way out

questions.question: Wind is described as 'the planet settling a debt' because:
options: The tropics collect a permanent surplus of energy and the poles a permanent shortfall, so winds and currents carry the surplus to the shortfall

questions.question: In the kitchen version, 'standing next to a braai and feeling the heat on your face' is:
The churning of the pap in the pot stands for convection, and in the atmosphere it explains:
options: Sea fog on the west coast
Hot afternoons on the Highveld building thunderclouds as warm air rises and cooler air sinks to replace it
The reflection of sunlight by snow

questions.question: 'The stove is under the pot, not above it' means:
options: The sun is below the horizon at night
The atmosphere is heated from BELOW by the ground, which is why climbers get colder as they climb even though they are getting closer to the sun
The ground is colder than the air

questions.question: The four kitchen words for the four heat-transfer processes are:
options: Braai, handle, churn, breeze — radiation, conduction, convection, advection

subtopics.title: Why Upington Bakes and Sutherland Freezes

questions.question: The torch analogy explains which factor?
options: LATITUDE — a torch shone straight down gives a small bright circle, a tilted torch smears the same light over a wide dim patch

questions.question: 'Water is a slow cooker and land is a frying pan' explains why:
options: The coast never goes to extremes — Durban is mild in July and not brutal in January — while the deep interior swings hard between the seasons

questions.question: Cloud is called 'a blanket that works both shifts' because it:
options: Keeps the DAY cooler by blocking sun and the NIGHT warmer by holding heat in, so cloudy places have small daily ranges and clear Karoo skies give scorching days and freezing nights

questions.question: In South Africa, the slope that catches most sun and is warmest and driest faces:
options: NORTH — the southern hemisphere is the mirror of the north, which is why orchards are sited there
